judged() removal: no test became vacuous. Every site that lost `assertThat(verdict.judged())` retained an isEmpty/containsExactly assertion on the violation list (ReaderInvariantsTest.aReaderThatSTOPSAtTheSealViolatesNothing:96, theREALReaderAppliesNothingBeyondTheSeal:167). No existing assertion was weakened; ReaderInvariantsScopeTest.theZOMBIEOnANeverOpenedChainIsStillReportedByCheckChain:139 was STRENGTHENED from judged()==false to containsExactly("I3").

findings.finding: The empty-epoch arm is judged only in the CLEAN direction, so half the hole this row exists to close can be reinstated with the whole suite green. anEpochWithNOObjectsAtAllIsJudgedAgainstItsInheritedBaseToo builds one reader shape (correct, RA=3) and asserts `isEmpty()`. A checker that DECLINES on this arm also returns an empty list, so the assertion cannot tell 'examined and clean' from 'not examined'. The `Verdict` type was the only thing that could distinguish them, and it was removed in this commit; the sister test on the seal-at-slot-0 arm compensates by asserting I4 and I3 for a broken reader, and this one does not.
The assertion description is off by one: `.as("epoch 9 inherits epoch 1's three records through six dead epochs")`. Epochs 2,3,4,5,6,7,8 have no objects -- seven dead epochs, not six.
findings.failure_scenario: The walk depth is the only thing this test distinguishes from the one-hop case, so a reader who trusts the description miscounts what the fixture covers and writes the next multi-hop test against the wrong span. The failure message printed when the test breaks names a span the store does not contain.
